delivered.name: ND Nr. 29 Rotbuche im Kramer Klett Park
delivered.access: Free, public city park (Cramer-Klett-Park, Wöhrd district; city-owned since 1929, opened to the public in 1931, renovated 2019)
delivered.transport: Short walk from Wöhrd district, roughly 15-20 min from Nuremberg Hauptbahnhof/Altstadt; specific tram/bus stop not verified
delivered.verify_notes: Registered as Naturdenkmal Nr. 29 (ND-05055) on the city's 2020 official Naturdenkmal ordinance, a European beech (Rotbuche) in Cramer-Klett-Park. Distinct from its neighbour ND-05054/Nr.28 (also a Rotbuche, still a lead, not shipped): the German Wikipedia list of Nuremberg's Naturdenkmäler gives ND-28 and ND-29 separate register IDs, separate coordinates roughly 80m apart (28: 49.45466/11.09082 with a Commons photo 'Fagus sylvatica EDA 1619.jpg' attached to that entry only; 29: 49.45482/11.08976, no photo listed), so these are two distinct specimens, not one tree double-counted. The park's own history is independently confirmed by German Wikipedia's Cramer-Klett-Park article: the Cramer-Klett family's 19th-century private garden, bought by the city in 1929, opened to the public in 1931, badly damaged in WWII, renovated 2019. That same Wikipedia Naturdenkmal-list page states plainly that only two of Nuremberg's Naturdenkmäler have died of fungal infection: a Rotbuche at the Laufer Schlagturm and a Blutbuche (copper beech, a different tree/cultivar, register Nr. 27) in this same park; Nr. 28 and Nr. 29 are not named among the dead, consistent with both still appearing on the live 2020 ordinance. No individual girth, age or description found for Nr. 29 specifically; flagged for that gap, not for doubt about the tree's existence or status. Species is beech (Fagus sylvatica) per the register name Rotbuche; if a future pass photographs it, girth should be recorded.

blocked.name: The 2019 additions to the Egmont inventory (Sophora japonica, Fraxinus excelsior f. pendula, Gleditsia triacanthos var. inermis)
blocked.reason: Already published, not new candidates. These three are bru_028 (Pagoda Tree, register entry 7111), bru_029 (Weeping Ash, entry 7109) and bru_030 (Thornless Honey Locust, entry 7110), all live in data/cities/brussels.json with distinct stories, location_precision approximate (shared 2019-survey coordinate 50.83777/4.35714), girth of up to 164cm recorded as a group maximum. The stale data/leads/brussels.json entry that resurfaced them has been removed from leads and logged in that file's own blocked list so it cannot re-fool a future pass. Parc d'Egmont's public status (free, daily 08:00-20:00) is already confirmed on the shipped entries; no further action needed.

blocked.name: Asken i Grundfor (Ash of Grundfor)
blocked.reason: Day-trip boundary fails. Dendron.dk (Individual_ID=1249, well-documented as of June 2019) confirms the tree, a European Ash 5.52m girth/23m tall on the northern hedge of Grundfor Praestegardshave, Skolestien 2 (matching the brief's coordinates exactly). The access question actually resolves FAVOURABLY: the former parsonage is now Hinnerup parish's shared church office (kirkekontor), open to the public Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri 09:00-12:30, so this is not a private home (confirmed via dinavis.dk and kirkenihinnerup.dk). But Grundfor itself is a small hamlet roughly 3-4km beyond Hinnerup station, the nearest rail stop, and no direct frequent bus link from Hinnerup to Grundfor could be confirmed in the time available; the realistic total journey from Aarhus centre (11-15 min train to Hinnerup, plus an unconfirmed onward leg) is very unlikely to land inside the ~30-minute public-transport day-trip boundary this project uses, and could not be verified to. Blocked on the day-trip rule rather than access; a future pass with a real Rejseplanen door-to-door time or confirmation of an infrequent bus/school-bus link could reopen this.
